newsitem.title: INDIA: India unifies operations to fight Assam insurgency.
newsitem.headline: India unifies operations to fight Assam insurgency.

text.p: A recent upsurge of violence in India's northeastern state of Assam has prompted the federal government to combine the military, paramilitary and state police forces under a single command, officials said on Monday.

The move, aimed at controlling growing separatist violence in the tea and oil-rich state, followed the explosion of two bombs under a train on December 30 that killed at least 33 people in western Assam.
The Bodoland Liberation Tigers Force (BLTF) said the group carried out the bomb attack because the government had refused to take up its demand for a separate tribal state.
A senior state government official told Reuters by telephone from the state capital Guwahati that security forces held their first meeting under the unified command on Monday.
India's northeast is made up of seven states, home to more than 200 ethnic groups fighting for a separate homeland.
"We will see how the unified command structure functions for the next three months and then we will decide whether to continue with it," said C.P. Mishra, a senior state official.
The unified command will have a three tier-structure, with strategy headed by the state's top civil servant, Mishra said.
The top army officer, Lt-Gen R.K. Sawhney, will handle overall operations, while senior district officials will coordinate operations at the village level.
India's northeast is surrounded by Burma, Bangladesh, Tibet and Bhutan. A 20-km (12-mile) land corridor links it to the Indian mainland through the eastern state of West Bengal.
In 1990, the army launched its first counter-insurgency operations against Assamese guerrillas, some of whom have been fighting for a sovereign country since 1979.

"Serious incidents of violence are taking place in the state, people are being killed, besides ambushed and extortions. The central government must do something," Home (Interior) Minister Indrajit Gupta said in Guwahati on Saturday.

But the ruling Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) party, five of its allies including two Communist parties and the state's two major opposition parties all opposed the strengthening of the army's role in counter-insurgency operations.
The AGP is a member of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left federal government.
